info.title: Flex API
info.description:
Flex's tenant API for integrations and AI agents. Every response is scoped to the organization that owns the presented key.

**Authentication.** Send `Authorization: Bearer flx_live_…` on every request. Keys are created by an organization administrator inside Flex; the secret is shown once and stored hashed. A key belongs to exactly one organization.

**Permissions.** A key is granted a subset of Flex permissions when it is created. Each endpoint states the permission it needs; a key without it receives 403. `GET /api/v1/modules` lists the permissions of the presented key.

**Modules.** Endpoints that belong to an optional Flex module (scheduling, invoicing, …) answer 403 with a problem detail when the organization has not activated that module. `GET /api/v1/modules` shows which modules are active.

**Rate limits.** Fixed one-minute windows, per key (default 120 requests/min, configurable per key) and per organization (600/min). Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the key's window resets) so a client can pace itself. Exceeding either limit returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds).

**Pagination.** List endpoints return `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor": "…" }`. Pass `after=<nextCursor>` to fetch the next page and `limit` to size it (1–200, default 50). `nextCursor` is null on the last page; cursors are opaque and stable.

**CSV.** Every list endpoint (`GET /api/v1/activity`, `/categories`, `/customers`, `/customers/{id}/locations`, `/jobs`, `/jobs/{id}/photos`, `/invoices`, `/items`, `/items/low-stock`, `/items/{id}/reorder-points`, `/items/{id}/units`, `/labor-rates`, `/locations`, `/purchase-orders`, `/reorder-points`, `/roles`, `/sales-orders`, `/schedule`, `/schedule-groups`, `/transfers`, `/users`, `/users/removal-requests`, `/vendors`) also answers in CSV: send `Accept: text/csv` or append `?format=csv`. Columns are the JSON property names in declaration order — a nested object is flattened to `parent.child` columns, a list of scalars is `;`-joined, a list of objects is compact JSON in the cell; values are written exactly as in the JSON (invariant decimals, ISO-8601 UTC dates, enum names, `true`/`false`, empty for null). The file is UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting, and a text cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR is prefixed with an apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run it as a formula. Paging is identical to JSON; because the CSV body has no envelope the next page's cursor is returned in the `X-Next-Cursor` header together with `Link: <next page URL>; rel="next"` (absent on the last page). Responses are attachments named `<resource>.csv`. `GET /api/v1/modules` and single-resource GETs are JSON only.

**ETags.** Single-resource and list GETs return a weak `ETag`. Send it back as `If-None-Match` to receive 304 Not Modified with no body when nothing changed. A list's tag is per representation — the JSON and CSV tags of the same page differ — and list responses carry `Vary: Accept`.

**Idempotency.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (any unique string, up to 128 characters) on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. Replaying the same key with the same body returns the original response instead of repeating the write; the same key with a different body is rejected with 422. Keys are remembered for 24 hours per organization.

**Errors.** Failures are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`: 400 validation errors list per-field messages under `errors`; 401/403/404/409/422/429/500 carry `title`, `detail` and a `traceId` to quote in support requests.

servers.description: Production — your organization's data, keys from Settings → Integrations → API Keys

Sandbox — demo organization, public read-only and write keys, reset nightly at 08:00 UTC. No real-world side effects: email, webhook delivery and automation actions don't run (automation rules match and are logged as skipped), and the AI assistant answers from a fixed demo script

get.summary: Lists logged API and MCP requests, oldest first, one page at a time.
get.description:
Requires `ManageOrganizations`. Rows are returned in the order they were written
(ascending `id`), so a poller can pass the last `nextCursor` back as
`after` to receive only newer rows. A row is written just after its response is
sent, so a request appears a moment after it completes. Rows are kept 90 days.
Example: `GET /api/v1/activity?since=2026-09-22T00:00:00Z&search=update_job_status`.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only requests that started at/after this instant (ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. `2026-09-22T00:00:00Z`).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Only requests that started before this instant (ISO-8601 UTC, exclusive).

parameters.name: apiKeyId
parameters.description: Only requests made with this key id. Example: `3`.

parameters.name: statusClass
parameters.description: Only responses of this HTTP status class, 1-5: e.g. `2` for 2xx, `4` for 4xx (1xx is accepted but never logged). Omit for all.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the path, MCP method and MCP tool name. Example: `jobs`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor` (a log row id). Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1..500 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

200.description: One page of log rows and the cursor for the next page (null on the last page).

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

get.summary: Lists the organization's item categories, one page at a time.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. Categories are flat with a `parentCategoryId`; nest them
client-side. The built-in system category is not listed. Example:
`GET /api/v1/categories?parentCategoryId=0` returns the top-level categories.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the name, e.g. `lum`.

parameters.name: parentCategoryId
parameters.description: Only direct children of this category; `0` for top-level categories only.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only categories created or edited at/after this UTC instant (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: SyncId of the last category of the previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

post.summary: Creates an item category.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "New Category" on
the Item Categories page, with stricter checks: the name must be unique among the categories
with the same parent, and the parent must be one of your categories that is neither the
built-in "No Category" nor Template Builder-generated. The new category has no properties.
Example: `{ "name": "Hardwood", "parentCategoryId": 1 }`.

requestBody.description: Name plus optional description and parent.

201.description: Created; body is the new category, `Location` points at it.

400.description: Malformed body, missing or blank `name`, a field over its limit, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

409.description: A category with this name already exists under the same parent, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: No such (usable) parent category, including a negative `parentCategoryId` (the field is listed in `errors`); or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

delete.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "Delete" on the
Item Categories page: only a category without child categories can be deleted (move or
delete them first). Its properties and its item assignments go with it; items whose primary
`categoryId` it was move to the organization's default "No Category". Items keep the
property values they already carry. Template Builder-generated categories
(`isTemplateBuilderCategory` = true) are removed by deleting their Template Builder, not here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category id. Example: `4`.

404.description: No such category in this organization.

409.description: The category has child categories, is Template Builder-generated, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

get.summary: Returns one item category.
get.description: Requires `ViewInventory`. Send the previous `ETag` as `If-None-Match` to receive `304 Not Modified` when unchanged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category id. Example: `4`.

404.description: No such category in this organization.

patch.summary: Renames, re-describes or moves an item category; only the fields sent change.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as editing the
category (or dragging it in the tree) on the Item Categories page. Moving a category
(`parentCategoryId`; `0` = top level) is refused when it would create a cycle, and
recalculates every item's inherited parent categories. Template Builder-generated categories
are managed by their Template Builder and cannot be changed here.
Example: `{ "name": "Softwood", "parentCategoryId": 0 }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category id. Example: `4`.

requestBody.description: The fields to change; at least one.

400.description: Empty body (no field to change), malformed body, a field over its limit, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such category in this organization.

409.description: The category is Template Builder-generated, another category under the (new) parent already has the name, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Blank name, no such (usable) parent, or the parent is the category itself or one of its descendants (the field is listed in `errors`); or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

get.summary: Lists a category's properties — its own and those inherited from parent categories.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. Ordered by `displayOrder`; inherited properties carry
`isInherited` and the defining `categoryId`. Supports `If-None-Match`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category id. Example: `4`.

404.description: No such category in this organization.

post.summary: Adds a property to a category.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "Add Property"
on the category's Manage Properties page, with typed validation: the default value must fit
`dataType` (and be among `options` for list types), options are only for
`Dropdown` / `MultiSelect`. A property with a parent category's name overrides it
(`overridesParent`). Existing items are not changed.
Example: `{ "name": "Species", "dataType": "Dropdown", "options": ["Pine", "Oak"], "defaultValue": "Pine" }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category id. Example: `4`.

201.description: Created; body is the category's properties (the new one included). `Location` points at the list.

400.description: Malformed body, missing `name`, a field over its limit, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such category in this organization.

409.description: The category already has a property with this name, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Reserved name, a default value that does not fit the type or options, invalid options, or a negative `displayOrder` (the field is listed in `errors`); or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

delete.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "Delete" on the
Manage Properties page: the definition goes; items that already carry the property keep it.
Only a property defined on this category can be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category id. Example: `4`.

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: Property id from GET (not inherited). Example: `57`.

200.description: Deleted; body is the category's remaining properties.

404.description: No such category, or no such property defined on it.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server.

patch.summary: Changes a category property; only the fields sent change.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as editing the
property on the Manage Properties page, as a partial update with the create rules. Only a
property defined on this category can be changed (an inherited one is edited on its own
category). Items that already carry the property keep their copy (name, type and value).
Example: `{ "defaultValue": "Oak", "displayOrder": 2 }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category id. Example: `4`.

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: Property id from GET (not inherited). Example: `57`.

requestBody.description: The fields to change; at least one.

200.description: Changed; body is the category's properties.

400.description: Empty body (no field to change), malformed body, a field over its limit, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such category, or no such property defined on it.

409.description: Another property of the category already has the name, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Blank or reserved name, a default value that does not fit the (new) type or options, invalid options, or a negative `displayOrder`; or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

get.summary: Lists customers, oldest first, one page at a time.
get.description:
Cursor pagination: pass the `nextCursor` of the previous response as
`after`. Filters combine with AND. Example:
`GET /api/v1/customers?isActive=true&updatedSince=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z&limit=100`.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: SyncId of the last item of the previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–200 (default 50).

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only customers created or edited at/after this UTC instant (ISO-8601, e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`).

parameters.name: isActive
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or deactivated (`false`) customers; omit for both.

parameters.name: customerType
parameters.description: Only this type: `EndCustomer`, `Installer`, `Distributor` or `Commercial`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only this status flag: `None`, `Preferred` or `Difficult`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against name, company name and e-mail.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

400.description: Malformed `after` cursor or filter value (validation problem listing the field).

post.summary: Creates a customer.
post.description:
Requires `ManageCustomers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header (unique per attempt;
a retry with the same key and body replays the first response). The customer is created
active with a zero balance; `country` defaults to `"USA"`; when any of
`address`/`city`/`state`/`postalCode` is given, a "Primary Address"
mailing location is created too (see `/customers/{id}/locations`). The write is
attributed to the user who created the API key.

201.description: The new customer; `Location` points at `/api/v1/customers/{id}`.

400.description: Malformed body, unknown enum value, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

409.description: The key's creator no longer exists on this server, so the write cannot be attributed.

422.description: Well-formed but invalid field values (problem lists the fields), or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

500.description: The customer could not be saved.

delete.description:
Requires `ManageCustomers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. This is the same
soft delete as the Customers page: the customer disappears from every list and lookup
(GETs answer 404) but keeps its history, and a user can restore it from
Customers → Deleted Customers in the app. The delete is refused with `409` while
the customer still has active jobs (not Completed/Cancelled), unpaid invoices
(not Paid/Cancelled) or active sales orders — complete or cancel those first; the
problem `detail` names which. To merely hide a customer from pickers without
deleting it, `PUT` it with `isActive: false` instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id.

200.description: The customer was deleted; body carries its id and a confirmation message.

404.description: No such customer in this organization (also for already-deleted customers).

409.description: Active jobs, unpaid invoices or active sales orders reference the customer, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The customer could not be saved.

get.summary: Returns one customer.
get.description: Send the previous `ETag` as `If-None-Match` to receive `304 Not Modified` when unchanged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id from a list response.

404.description: No such customer in this organization (also for deleted customers).

put.summary: Replaces the editable fields of one customer.
put.description:
Requires `ManageCustomers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. This is a full
update: every editable field takes the value in the body (omitted optional fields
become null / defaults), so GET the customer first and send it back modified.
Optional optimistic concurrency: send the `ETag` from that GET as `If-Match`
to get `412` instead of overwriting a change made in the meantime.
Balances, deletion state and audit fields cannot be changed here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id.

requestBody.description: The complete set of editable fields.

400.description: Malformed body, unknown enum value, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such customer in this organization (also for deleted customers).

409.description: Concurrent edit detected, or the key's creator no longer exists on this server.

412.description: `If-Match` does not match the customer's current `ETag`.

422.description: Well-formed but invalid field values (problem lists the fields), or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

500.description: The customer could not be saved.

get.summary: Lists the additional locations (job sites / addresses) of one customer.
get.description:
The customer's primary address is on the customer resource itself; this collection
holds the extra sites jobs can be booked at. Cursor-paginated like every list.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: SyncId of the last item of the previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–200 (default 50).

parameters.name: isActive
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or retired (`false`) locations; omit for both.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

200.description: A page of locations (may be empty).

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

404.description: No such customer in this organization.

post.summary: Adds a location (job site / address) to a customer.
post.description:
Requires `ManageCustomers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same rules as
Customers → Addresses → Add in the app: `name`, `address`, `city`, `state`
and `postalCode` are required; `isMailingAddress: true` moves the mailing flag here
from the customer's other locations, and a customer's first location is always the mailing
address. Attributed to the user who created the API key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id.

201.description: The new location; `Location` points at `/api/v1/customers/{id}/locations/{locationId}`.

400.description: Malformed body, a field over its length limit, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such customer in this organization (also for deleted customers).

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server, so the write cannot be attributed.

422.description: A required field is missing; the fields are listed in `errors`.

delete.description:
Requires `ManageCustomers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The same delete as the
Customers → Addresses page: the location is deactivated (`isActive: false`) rather than
erased, so it stays on history and disappears from pickers; restore it with a PATCH of
`isActive: true`. Refused with `409` while any job (in any status) references it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Location id.

200.description: The location was retired; body carries its id and a confirmation message.

404.description: No such customer in this organization, or the location belongs to another customer.

409.description: Jobs reference the location (the detail says how many), or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

get.summary: Returns one location of a customer.
get.description: Send the previous `ETag` as `If-None-Match` to receive `304 Not Modified` when unchanged; send it as `If-Match` on a PATCH to avoid overwriting a concurrent edit.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Location id from the customer's location list.

404.description: No such customer in this organization, or the location belongs to another customer.

patch.summary: Edits a customer location; only the fields sent change.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageCustomers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. `""` clears an optional
field; `name`, `address`, `city`, `state` and `postalCode` cannot be cleared.
`isMailingAddress: true` unmarks the customer's other locations; `isActive` retires or
restores the location. Optional optimistic concurrency: send the `ETag` from
`GET …/locations/{locationId}` as `If-Match` to get `412` instead of overwriting a
change made in the meantime. Example: `PATCH /api/v1/customers/5/locations/9 { "notes": "Gate code 4411" }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Customer id.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Location id.

400.description: Malformed body, a field over its length limit, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such customer in this organization, or the location belongs to another customer.

409.description: Concurrent edit detected, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

412.description: `If-Match` does not match the location's current `ETag`.

422.description: A required field was cleared; the fields are listed in `errors`.

get.summary: Lists invoice headers.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInvoices`. Cursor-paginated: pass the last invoice's `syncId`
as `after`.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only invoices in this status (name such as `Sent` or numeric value).

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Only invoices billing this job.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Only invoices billed to this customer.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only invoices created or modified at/after this UTC instant.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: SyncId of the last invoice of the previous page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1..200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

post.summary: Creates a standalone invoice (not tied to a job) from explicit lines.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The subtotal is
the sum of the lines; tax applies to all of it at `taxRate` (0 for a tax-exempt
customer). Every omitted field defaults exactly as the New Invoice page does (next
`INV-SA-…` number, today, the organization's default payment terms, tax rate and
payment instructions). Like that page, the invoice is created already finalized
(status `Sent`) — there is no draft step — so a payment can be recorded at once
with `POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/payments`. To bill a job instead, use
`POST /api/v1/invoices/from-job`.

requestBody.description: Customer, lines and, optionally, how to bill.

201.description: The new invoice; `Location` points at it.

400.description: Malformed body, no lines, or an out-of-range value.

409.description: The invoice number is already used, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Unknown `customerId` or `customerAddressId`, or `dueDate` precedes `invoiceDate`.

500.description: The invoice could not be saved.

delete.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. The API twin of
the draft invoice page's "Delete Draft" button. Only a `Draft` can be deleted — a
finalized invoice is voided instead (`POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/void`). A consolidated
draft, or a draft carrying a payment other than the job's transferred down payment, is refused.
Money goes back where it came from: the job's down payment returns to the job (the next
invoice re-applies it), applied store credit returns to the customer, and the job's or sales
order's payment status is recalculated. A job moved from `Completed` to `Invoiced` by
generating this draft goes back to `Completed` when no other non-voided invoice remains
(counter-sales organizations keep `Invoiced`); its stock movements stay, and the job can
simply be invoiced again (`POST /api/v1/invoices/from-job`).
Deletion is permanent — there is no restore, and the invoice, its lines, payments and notes
disappear from every synced device. Fires `invoice.deleted`. Repeating the request with the
same `Idempotency-Key` replays the 204; a new key for an already-deleted id gets 404.
The deletion is recorded on the job's history, attributed to the user who created the key.
Example: `DELETE /api/v1/invoices/57`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric invoice id, e.g. `57`.

204.description: The draft invoice was deleted; no body.

404.description: No such invoice in the calling organization (or it was already deleted).

409.description: The invoice is not a draft (void it instead), is a consolidated invoice, has recorded payments, or the key's creator is unknown on this server — the `detail` says which.

500.description: The deletion could not be saved.

get.summary: Returns one invoice with its lines and payments.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInvoices`. `id` may be the numeric id or the `syncId`.
Sends a weak `ETag`; repeat with `If-None-Match` to get 304 when unchanged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric id or SyncId.

404.description: No such invoice in the calling organization.

patch.summary: Edits a draft invoice's header (number, dates, terms, notes, payment instructions, tax rate).
patch.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. PATCH semantics: only the
fields you send change. Only a `Draft` invoice can be edited (a finalized invoice is
immutable — void it and issue a new one). Totals are not editable here: the subtotal comes
from the job, so recompute it with `POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/refresh-from-job` after the
job's lines change. The write is attributed to the user who created the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric invoice id.

400.description: Malformed body, missing `Idempotency-Key`, or a tax rate out of 0–100.

404.description: No such invoice in the calling organization.

409.description: The invoice is not a draft, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: The invoice number was sent blank.

post.summary: Finalizes a draft invoice (marks it sent).
post.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Freezes the
draft's lines, records the send and moves it to `Sent` — the same step as the
"Finalize" button, minus the customer email (send that through your own channel using
`GET /api/v1/invoices/{id}`). Calling it on an already-finalized invoice only
refreshes its audit fields and returns it unchanged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric invoice id.

404.description: No such invoice in the calling organization.

409.description: The invoice is voided or was consolidated into another invoice, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

post.summary: Records a payment and/or applies store credit to an invoice.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same rules as the
Record Payment dialog: at least one of `amount` or store credit is required, a
payment needs a `paymentMethod`, and the total may not exceed the balance due
(extra money belongs in store credit, not on the invoice). Only a finalized invoice
takes payments — a draft must be marked sent first; a consolidated member is paid
through the consolidated invoice. The invoice moves to `PartiallyPaid` or
`Paid` (which fires `invoice.paid`), and the job's or sales order's payment
status follows. Returns the updated invoice; the payment itself appears in
`GET /api/v1/invoices/{id}`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric invoice id.

requestBody.description: Amount, method and reference, and/or store credit to apply.

404.description: No such invoice in the calling organization.

409.description: The invoice is a draft or was consolidated into another invoice, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Nothing to apply, a payment without a method, or the payment exceeds the balance due.

500.description: The payment could not be saved.

post.summary: Recomputes a draft invoice's total from its job's current unbilled amount.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Same as the
app's "Update draft from job": after you change the job's lines (materials, labor, charges),
this refreshes the draft's subtotal to the job's remaining unbilled amount (including any
retroactive tier credits). Only a `Draft` invoice that bills a job. The write is
attributed to the user who created the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric invoice id.

200.description: The refreshed invoice with its updated subtotal and total.

404.description: No such invoice in the calling organization.

409.description: The invoice is not a draft or is not linked to a job, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

post.summary: Voids an invoice.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same rules as the
Void button: only a finalized invoice with no recorded payments can be voided (delete
or refund its payments first); a draft is not voided but deleted
(`DELETE /api/v1/invoices/{id}`); a consolidated invoice is voided as a whole, not
through its members. Applied store credit is handed back to the
customer and the job's payment status is recalculated. Voiding is permanent — the
invoice stays visible with status `Cancelled`. The body is optional.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric invoice id.

requestBody.description: Optional reason, recorded on the job.

404.description: No such invoice in the calling organization.

409.description: Already voided, a draft (delete it with `DELETE /api/v1/invoices/{id}` instead), consolidated, has recorded payments, or the key's creator is unknown on this server — the `detail` says which.

post.summary: Creates a draft invoice for a job.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInvoices` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Bills the job's
full price — or, once a finalized invoice exists, only its unbilled remainder (a
supplemental invoice). The job's down payment transfers onto the invoice; store credit
is applied when requested. Every omitted field defaults exactly as the Generate Invoice
page does. The result is a `Draft`: finalize it with
`POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/mark-sent`, or discard it with
`DELETE /api/v1/invoices/{id}` (a pending draft blocks a second one).

requestBody.description: What to bill and, optionally, how.

201.description: The new draft invoice; `Location` points at it.

404.description: No such job in the calling organization.

409.description: The job cannot be invoiced (cancelled, estimate option not chosen), a draft is already pending, the invoice number is taken, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Nothing left to bill, or `dueDate` precedes `invoiceDate`.

500.description: The invoice could not be saved.

get.summary: Lists items (templates) with pricing and total on-hand.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. Draft and deleted templates are excluded.
Cursor-paginated: pass the last item's `syncId` as `after`.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against name and description.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Only items in this category (primary or assigned).

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only items created or updated at/after this UTC instant.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: SyncId of the last item of the previous page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1..200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

post.summary: Creates a catalog item.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as adding an
item in the app: the item gets the organization's default "No Category" when
`categoryId` is omitted, its `Cost` and `Unit Price` properties are
created (0 unless `cost` / `unitPrice` are supplied, stored to 2 decimals) and
the category's properties are copied onto it. An active item with the same name is
refused with `409` (the rule the app's template builder applies). Creates no stock —
follow up with `POST /api/v1/items/{id}/stock/adjust`. No webhook fires for a
create. Permissions mirror the app exactly: the Items page creates items, sets price/cost
and category under `ManageInventory`, so that is all this endpoint needs — except
`description`, which in the app is edited only on the Item Templates page and so
additionally requires `ManageTemplates` (`403` otherwise; omit the field or
grant the permission to the key).
Example: `{ "name": "1/2\" PEX Coupling", "categoryId": 4, "unitPrice": 1.25, "cost": 0.40 }`.

requestBody.description: Name plus optional description, category, starting price and cost.

201.description: Created; body is the item exactly as `GET /api/v1/items/{id}` returns it, `Location` points at it.

400.description: Malformed body, missing `name`, out-of-range value, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

403.description: The key lacks `ManageInventory`, or it sent `description` without holding `ManageTemplates`.

409.description: An active item with this name already exists, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: No such category in this organization (`categoryId`), or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

500.description: The item could not be saved; nothing was created.

delete.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as
"Deactivate" on the Items page: the item leaves the catalogue and this API (GETs answer
404), its physical inventory rows and history are untouched, and a user can restore it
from Items → Deactivated Items in the app. A parent group that still contains active
items is refused with `409`; repeat with `?cascadeChildren=true` to deactivate
the group and its items together (each restorable individually).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

parameters.name: cascadeChildren
parameters.description: For a parent group: also deactivate its active child items instead of refusing.

200.description: The item was deactivated; body carries its id and a confirmation (mentions cascaded children when any).

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

409.description: The group still contains active items and `cascadeChildren` was not set, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

get.summary: Returns one item with its properties, price tiers, barcodes and per-location stock.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. `id` may be the numeric id or the `syncId`.
Sends a weak `ETag`; repeat with `If-None-Match` to get 304 when unchanged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric id or SyncId.

404.description: No such item in the calling organization.

patch.summary: Changes some of an item's name, description, category, price, cost, preferred vendor or vendor part number.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Partial update:
only the fields present in the body change; omitted (or `null`) fields are left
alone, and `"description": ""` (or whitespace only) clears the description. The same rules as the Items
page apply — renaming also renames every inventory unit of the item; a new
`unitPrice` / `cost` is written to the item and its future stock only
(existing units keep their own pricing, as with "push to existing inventory" left off);
changing `categoryId` copies that category's properties onto the item. A rename to
an active item's name is refused with `409`. Optional optimistic concurrency: send
the `ETag` from `GET /api/v1/items/{id}` as `If-Match` to get `412`
instead of overwriting a change made in the meantime (the tag covers stock too, so a
concurrent stock move also yields 412 — GET again and retry). Fires the
`item.updated` webhook naming the changed fields. Permissions mirror the app
exactly: name, price/cost and category are edited on the Items page under
`ManageInventory`; `description` is edited only on the Item Templates page, so
sending it (including `""` to clear) additionally requires `ManageTemplates`
(`403` otherwise, nothing changed). The same applies to `preferredVendorId`
(an active vendor of the organization; `0` removes the link) and
`vendorPartNumber` (`""` clears it), which the app edits on Item Templates → Edit;
an unknown or inactive vendor is `422`.
Example: `{ "unitPrice": 1.35 }` or `{ "preferredVendorId": 3, "vendorPartNumber": "PX-12C" }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

requestBody.description: The fields to change; at least one.

200.description: Updated; body is the item exactly as `GET /api/v1/items/{id}` returns it.

400.description: Empty body (no field to change), malformed body, out-of-range value, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

403.description: The key lacks `ManageInventory`, or it sent `description`, `preferredVendorId` or `vendorPartNumber` without holding `ManageTemplates`.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

409.description: An active item with the new name already exists, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

412.description: `If-Match` does not match the item's current `ETag`.

422.description: Blank `name`, no such category in this organization (`categoryId`), no such active vendor (`preferredVendorId`), or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

500.description: The item could not be saved; nothing changed.

get.summary: Lists the categories an item is in, and which of them are assigned to it by hand.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. An item is in the categories assigned to it by hand
(`assignedCategoryIds`), their parent categories, and those its Template Builder gives
it; its primary `categoryId` is shown separately. Supports `If-None-Match`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Item id. Example: `12`.

404.description: No such item in this organization.

delete.summary: Removes a hand-assigned category from an item.
delete.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as unticking the
category on the item's page; the item's categories are recalculated, so a parent category
stays while another assigned child needs it, and Template Builder categories always stay.
Removing a category that is not assigned by hand changes nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Item id. Example: `12`.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Category id from `assignedCategoryIds`. Example: `4`.

200.description: Removed; body is the item's categories.

404.description: No such item, or no such category, in this organization.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server.

post.summary: Assigns a category to an item.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as ticking the
category under Categories on the item's page: the item (and its inventory units) also get the
category's parent categories. Assigning an already assigned category changes nothing. The
built-in "No Category" and Template Builder-generated categories cannot be assigned by hand.
The item's primary `categoryId` is not changed (use `PATCH /api/v1/items/{id}`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Item id. Example: `12`.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Category id from `GET /api/v1/categories`. Example: `4`.

200.description: Assigned; body is the item's categories.

404.description: No such item, or no such category, in this organization.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: The category is the built-in "No Category" or Template Builder-generated; or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

get.summary: Lists an item's custom fields (properties) with definitions and current values.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. Returns every property of the item — custom fields plus the
pricing properties `Cost` and `Unit Price` (flagged `isPricing`) — ordered by
name, with its data type, options, whether it is calculated (read-only), item-level or
customized. Values are the item's (template's) values; each inventory unit carries a copy
that follows the item unless it was individually customized in the app.
Supports `If-None-Match`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

patch.summary: Sets several custom-field values of an item at once, by property name.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as editing values
in the Items page's item modal: a property that came from the Item Template becomes
"Customized" (`isCustomized`) and stops following the template, and each new value
flows to every inventory unit whose copy was not individually customized. Values are
checked against the property's type and options (Number: decimal like `"12.5"`;
Boolean: `"true"`/`"false"`; Date: `yyyy-MM-dd`; Dropdown: one option;
MultiSelect: comma-separated options; `""` clears). All or nothing: one unknown name,
invalid value, calculated or pricing property refuses the whole request. Calculated values
that depend on a changed property are recomputed in the same write, on the item and on its
inventory units (as in the modal). Fires `item.updated` (`changedFields``properties`, names in `changedProperties`).
Example: `{ "values": { "Color": "Red", "Length": "12" } }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

200.description: Values saved; body is the item's properties as GET returns them, `propagated` = inventory unit copies updated.

400.description: Malformed body, no values, more than 100 values, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

409.description: A named property is calculated or a pricing property (`Cost` / `Unit Price`), or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: A name matches no property of the item, a name is listed twice, or a value does not fit its property (the error is keyed `values[name]`); or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

post.summary: Adds an item-level custom field to an item.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "Add property"
in the Items page's item modal: the property belongs to this item only (`isItemLevel`;
the Item Template never changes it) and is also added, with the same value, to every
existing inventory unit that lacks it (new stock copies it automatically). The value is
checked against `dataType`. List types start without options; set them with
`PATCH .../properties/{propertyId}` (`ManageTemplates`).
Example: `{ "name": "Warranty (years)", "dataType": "Number", "value": "2" }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

requestBody.description: Name, data type and optional starting value.

201.description: Created; body is the item's properties (the new one included), `propagated` = inventory units it was added to. `Location` points at the list.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

409.description: The item already has a property with this name, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Reserved name (`Cost` / `Unit Price`), or the value does not fit `dataType`; or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

delete.summary: Deletes a property from an item.
delete.description:
Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header and the permission of the app page that deletes that
kind of property. An item-level property (`isItemLevel`) is deleted as in the Items
page's item modal (`ManageInventory`): the copies on inventory units that were not
individually customized are removed with it. Any other property is deleted as on the Item
Templates page (`ManageTemplates`): the item's property goes, inventory units keep
their copies. Either way a property referenced by another property's calculation is refused
and the property's own calculation is removed; `Cost` and `Unit Price` can never be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: Property id from GET.

200.description: Deleted; body is the item's remaining properties, `propagated` = inventory unit copies removed.

403.description: The key lacks `ManageInventory` (item-level property) or `ManageTemplates` (any other property).

404.description: No such property on an active item in this organization.

409.description: The property is `Cost` / `Unit Price` or is referenced by another property's calculation, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

patch.summary: Changes a property's name, data type or options.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageTemplates` and an `Idempotency-Key` header — in the app a property's
definition is edited on the Item Templates page. Only the fields sent change, all in one
save (every field is validated first). Rules as on that page: names are unique on the item;
changing `dataType` clears the value unless the new type is `Text` and is refused
while the property has an enabled calculation. Additionally: options are allowed only for
`Dropdown` / `MultiSelect` and dropped when the type leaves them; `Cost` /
`Unit Price` cannot be changed and are reserved names. Inventory units keep their copies
under the old name / type (as with the page).
Example: `{ "dataType": "Dropdown", "options": ["Red", "Blue"] }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: Property id from GET.

requestBody.description: The fields to change; at least one.

200.description: Changed; body is the item's properties.

400.description: Empty body (no field to change), malformed body, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such property on an active item in this organization.

409.description: Another property already has the name, the type change is blocked by an enabled calculation, the property is `Cost` / `Unit Price`, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Blank or reserved name, options on a non-list type, or an invalid option (blank, comma, duplicate); or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

post.summary: Reverts a customized property to its Item Template default.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "Revert" in the
Items page's item modal: the value goes back to the Item Template's default (or its first
visible option, or empty), `isCustomized` clears so the property follows the template
again, and the value flows to inventory units like an edit. Only for properties that came
from the item's Item Template.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: Property id from GET.

200.description: Reverted; body is the item's properties.

404.description: No such property on an active item in this organization.

409.description: The property is item-level, the item is not assigned to an Item Template, the template no longer has the property, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

put.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Single-property form of
`PATCH /api/v1/items/{id}/properties` with the same rules (Customized flag, flow to
inventory units, dependent calculated values recomputed, typed validation, calculated and
pricing properties refused).
Example: `{ "value": "Red" }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: Property id from GET.

200.description: Value saved; body is the item's properties, `propagated` = inventory unit copies updated.

404.description: No such property on an active item in this organization.

409.description: The property is calculated or a pricing property, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: The value does not fit the property's type or options, or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

get.summary: Lists an item's reorder points.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. Every reorder point of the item, switched on or off: the
all-locations one first, then by location name. Not cursor-paginated: `nextCursor` is
always `null`. Example: `GET /api/v1/items/42/reorder-points`.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

put.summary: Creates or updates an item's reorder point for one location.
put.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The reorder point for
(item, `locationId`) is created, or updated when one exists — the oldest, if the
Thresholds page has made duplicates. Omit `locationId` for the rule on the item's
stock at all locations together. Same values and ranges as Reorder → Thresholds in the
app; send `"isActive": false` to switch it off. Takes effect at once for
`GET /api/v1/items/low-stock`. Example:
`{ "locationId": 3, "minimumStock": 10, "reorderQuantity": 24 }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

requestBody.description: Location, minimum stock, optional reorder quantity and on/off.

200.description: Updated an existing reorder point; body is it.

201.description: Created a reorder point; body is it.

400.description: Malformed body, missing or negative `minimumStock`, negative `reorderQuantity`, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: No such location in this organization (`locationId`), or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

post.summary: Adds or removes stock for an item at one location.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. A positive
`delta` creates that many stock units at the location exactly like "Add inventory"
on the Items page (template properties, cost, barcodes copied); a negative `delta`
writes off the oldest available units the way "Delete" on the Inventory page does
(soft delete - restorable in the app, recorded in each unit's change history with
`reason`). Stock never goes negative here: removing more than is on hand answers
`409` and changes nothing. Units in transit on a transfer are never touched.
Omit `locationId` for the organization's "No Location" bucket. Misc items, parent
groups and sub-unit items hold no stock (`409`); job sites are refused (`422`).
Example: `{ "locationId": 3, "delta": -2, "reason": "Damaged in van" }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

requestBody.description: Location, signed unit count and optional reason.

200.description: Stock changed; body carries the confirmation and the item's updated per-location stock.

400.description: Malformed body, `delta` of zero, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

409.description: Not enough units at the location to remove, the item cannot hold stock, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Unknown location, or the location is a job site.

post.summary: Moves stock for an item from one location to another.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Re-points
`quantity` of the oldest available units at `fromLocationId` to
`toLocationId` - the same thing as "Quick move" on the Inventory page, recorded in
each unit's change history. Nothing is created or destroyed; the item's total on hand is
unchanged. Fewer available units than requested answers `409` and moves nothing.
Omit `toLocationId` for the organization's "No Location" bucket. Job sites are refused
at either end (`422`) - stock reaches a job site through a job or a transfer.
Example: `{ "fromLocationId": 1, "toLocationId": 4, "quantity": 3 }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id.

requestBody.description: Source, destination, unit count and optional note.

200.description: Stock moved; body carries the confirmation and the item's updated per-location stock.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

409.description: Not enough units at the source, the item cannot hold stock, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Unknown location, a job site at either end, or source and destination are the same.

get.summary: Lists an item's inventory units with their per-unit property values, one page at a time.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. Every active unit is listed, including units in transit, at
job sites and in bundles (see `status`). Example:
`GET /api/v1/items/12/units?locationId=3` returns the units held at location 3.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`; `properties` is
one JSON cell); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id. Example: `12`.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Only units held at this location.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only units created or changed (including a custom-field value change) at/after this UTC instant (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: SyncId of the last unit of the previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

404.description: No such active item in this organization.

get.summary: Returns one inventory unit of an item with its property values.
get.description: Requires `ViewInventory`. Supports `If-None-Match`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id. Example: `12`.

parameters.name: unitId
parameters.description: Unit id from the list. Example: `5012`.

404.description: No such active item, or no such active unit of it.

put.summary: Sets one custom-field value on one inventory unit.
put.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as editing the
value on the unit's Inventory edit page: the unit's copy becomes customized
(`isCustomized`) and stops following the item's value, and the unit's calculated values
that read it are recomputed in the same write. Only this unit changes — to change the item
and every uncustomized unit use `PATCH /api/v1/items/{id}/properties`. The value is
checked against the property's type and options; calculated values and `Cost` /
`Unit Price` are refused. `{name}` is the property name, URL-encoded,
case-insensitive. Fires `item.updated` (`changedFields``unitProperties`).
Example: `PUT /api/v1/items/12/units/5012/properties/Color` with `{ "value": "Blue" }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric item id. Example: `12`.

parameters.name: unitId
parameters.description: Unit id from the list. Example: `5012`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Property name on the unit, e.g. `Color`.

200.description: Saved; body is the unit as GET returns it.

400.description: Malformed body, a value over 4000 characters, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such active item, unit, or property on the unit.

409.description: The property is calculated on this unit or is `Cost` / `Unit Price`, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: The value does not fit the property's type or options (keyed `value`); or `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body.

get.summary: Lists items below one of their reorder points, with on-hand, reorder quantity and vendor.
get.description:
Requires `ViewInventory`. One line per active reorder point whose watched stock is
strictly below its `minimumStock` — an item with reorder points at two locations can
appear twice. Stock is the count of non-deleted units at the reorder point's location, or
everywhere when it has none (the Reorder page's rule). `vendorId` is the item's
preferred vendor (set on Item Templates → Edit or `PATCH /api/v1/items/{id}`), else
the vendor of the CSV import that created it. Computed on request and read-only: unlike
opening the Reorder page it raises no alert and fires no `inventory.low_stock`
webhook. Ordered by item name then location. Not cursor-paginated (the list is bounded by
the reorder points): everything comes back with `nextCursor` always `null`.
Example: `GET /api/v1/items/low-stock?vendorId=3`.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: vendorId
parameters.description: Only lines whose resolved `vendorId` is this vendor; `0` = only lines with no vendor. Example: `3`.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Only reorder points watching this location. Example: `5`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

post.summary: Applies several stock adjustments and moves in one call, all or nothing.
post.description:
Requires `ManageInventory` and an `Idempotency-Key` header (one key covers the
whole batch). Each operation follows the rules of `POST /api/v1/items/{id}/stock/adjust`
(`"action": "Adjust"`) or `/stock/move` (`"action": "Move"`). Operations apply
in order, so a later removal can use units an earlier one added. Every operation is checked
before anything is written, and the writes share one transaction: if any operation fails,
nothing changes and the problem's `detail` starts with `operations[i]` naming the first
failing one (also in the `failedIndex` extension). 1..100 operations, at most 1000 units in total.
Example: <c>{ "operations": [ { "action": "Adjust", "itemId": 12, "locationId": 3, "delta": 10 },
{ "action": "Move", "itemId": 12, "fromLocationId": 3, "toLocationId": 4, "quantity": 2 } ] }</c>.

200.description: Every operation applied; one result per operation with the item's stock after the batch.

400.description: Malformed body, empty or oversized batch, an operation missing its `delta`/`quantity`, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: An operation names no active item in this organization.

409.description: Not enough units for an operation, an item that cannot hold stock, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Unknown location, a job site, source equal to destination, or too many units in total.

get.summary: Lists the organization's jobs, oldest first, one page at a time.
get.description:
Pagination: pass the previous response's `nextCursor` as `after`; `limit`
defaults to 50 and is capped at 200. All filters combine with AND. Response carries a
weak `ETag`; resend it as `If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Workflow status name to match exactly (case-insensitive), e.g. `Scheduled`, `InProgress`, `Completed`.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Only jobs for this customer id.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only jobs created or modified at or after this instant (ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`). Use it to poll for changes.

parameters.name: scheduledFrom
parameters.description: Only jobs whose scheduled start is at or after this local wall-clock time (`yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss`, no zone suffix).

parameters.name: scheduledTo
parameters.description: Only jobs whose scheduled start is at or before this local wall-clock time.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor` (a job SyncId). Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

200.description: A page of jobs and the cursor for the next page (null on the last page).

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

400.description: Unknown `status` or unusable `after` cursor (field listed in `errors`).

post.summary: Creates a job (estimate or draft) for a customer, optionally with material, labor and custom-charge lines.
post.description:
Same code path as the MVC "Create job" page. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`
header. Line totals are computed on the server from the lines you send. The job
number is generated when omitted. Initial status: `Estimated`, or `Draft`
when `isDraft` is true, unless `statusId` / `statusKey` names one of
the organization's statuses. `publishImmediately: true` is the "Create & Publish"
button: the job is created as a `Draft` and published in the same call under the
rules of `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/finalize`; when it cannot be published yet it is
still created as a `Draft` and the response's `warning` says why (never a 4xx
for an unpublishable-but-created job). The write is attributed to the user who created the key.

201.description: The created job (same shape as `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}`, plus `warning` when a requested publish did not happen); `Location` points at it.

400.description: Malformed body, missing `Idempotency-Key`, both `statusId` and `statusKey` given, or `publishImmediately` with a non-Draft status.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server, or the service refused the create.

422.description: Unknown customer, site address, status, item template, labor rate or task template for this organization (field listed in `errors`).

get.summary: Returns one job with its site address, pricing, assignees, material and labor lines and note timeline.
get.description:
Removed (soft-deleted) lines and assignments are excluded. Response carries a weak
`ETag`; resend it as `If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from the list endpoint.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

patch.summary: Edits a draft/estimate job's core fields (type, description, notes, schedule, customer, address). Status changes go through `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/status`.
patch.description:
PATCH semantics: only the fields you send change; omitted fields are left as they are.
Same rules as the web Edit page: only jobs in an editable status (Draft, Estimated,
Inspection in progress, Awaiting option selection) can be edited, and the customer,
address must belong to your organization. Status changes use `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/status`. Line items, labor and custom
charges are edited through their own endpoints, not here. Totals are never taken from the
caller — the job is repriced after the change, so a new customer's tax is applied.
Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header; the write is attributed to the user who created the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from `GET /api/v1/jobs`.

404.description: No job with this id in your organization.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: The job is not in an editable status, or the customer, address or status does not belong to your organization (the detail says which).

post.summary: Assigns people to a job — additively by default, or as the complete new crew with `replace: true`.
post.description:
Requires the Scheduling module. User ids come from `GET /api/v1/users` and must be
active members of the organization. People already on the job keep their crew
(schedule group) context; newly added people are assigned as individuals. With
`replace: true` anyone not listed is unassigned (an empty list clears the job).
Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from a list response.

requestBody.description: User ids to assign and whether they replace the current set.

200.description: Job id and a message listing who was assigned / unassigned (or "Assignments unchanged.").

403.description: Scheduling module not active for this organization.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: One or more `userIds` are not active members of this organization (listed in the message).

post.summary: Cancels a job, returning its materials to stock.
post.description:
Same rules as the UI: a job that has received payment, or has sent/paid invoices,
cannot be cancelled until the money is refunded / invoices voided (409). A job with
an uncollected down payment can be cancelled with `issueStoreCredit: true`
when the key holds `ManageStoreCredit`. Cancelling an already-cancelled job
answers 200 with a `warning`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from a list response.

requestBody.description: Optional reason and the store-credit choice.

200.description: Job id, confirmation message and an optional warning.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

409.description: Payments or invoices block the cancellation, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

post.summary: Adds a custom charge to a job (fees, disposal, permits …).
post.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. A cancelled job is
read-only. The write is attributed to the key's creator.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id.

404.description: No job with this id in your organization.

422.description: The job is cancelled or the charge is invalid (the detail says which).

delete.summary: Removes a custom charge from a job (soft delete).
delete.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. A charge on a
finalized invoice can't be deleted (use Return Items); a cancelled job is read-only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id.

parameters.name: chargeId
parameters.description: Custom-charge id.

200.description: The updated job with the charge removed.

404.description: No such job in your organization, or the charge is not one of its live charges.

422.description: The job is cancelled or the charge is billed (the detail says which).

patch.summary: Edits a custom charge's name, price and/or description.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. PATCH semantics. A charge
on a finalized invoice changes only through Return Items; a cancelled job is read-only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id.

parameters.name: chargeId
parameters.description: Custom-charge id (`customCharges[].id` of the job).

404.description: No such job in your organization, or the charge is not one of its live charges.

422.description: The job is cancelled or the charge is billed (the detail says which).

post.summary: Publishes a draft estimate.
post.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same rules as the
"Publish Estimate" button on the job page: only a `Draft` can be published, it
needs at least one charge (labor, material or custom) and every material line must
have a unit price. The job lands on `Estimated`, on `Scheduled` when a
scheduled date was already set while drafting, or on `AwaitingOptionSelection`
for a multi-option estimate; a history entry records the change. No body is required.
To create and publish in one call use `publishImmediately` on `POST /api/v1/jobs`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from a list response.

200.description: Job id and confirmation message (e.g. `Estimate published successfully! You can now send it to the customer.`).

404.description: No such job in this organization.

409.description: The job is not a draft, it has no charges / an unpriced material line, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The change could not be saved; nothing was changed. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Adds a material line to a job (the app's "Add material" button).
post.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same rules as the web
app: a cancelled job is read-only, parent / sell-by-unit / add-on items are added through
the app instead, and a matching plain planned line is merged rather than duplicated. The
line price is resolved by the pricing engine (tiers) unless you send a `unitPrice`
that differs from the base price, which is kept as a manual override. In counter-sales mode
stock is consumed immediately. The write is attributed to the user who created the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from `GET /api/v1/jobs`.

404.description: No job with this id in your organization.

422.description: The item template is unknown, not addable this way, or the job is cancelled (the detail says which).

delete.summary: Removes a material line from a job (soft delete).
delete.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Only Planned
lines (or counter-sales lines whose stock can be restored) can go; a line on an active
transfer or a finalized invoice can't — use Return Items for delivered goods. Totals are
recomputed. The write is attributed to the user who created the key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Material line id.

200.description: The updated job with the line removed.

404.description: No such job in your organization, or the line is not one of its live material lines.

422.description: The job is cancelled, the line is billed, on an active transfer, or not deletable (the detail says which).

patch.summary: Edits a material line's quantity, price and/or note.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. PATCH semantics: only the
fields you send change. Quantity changes only apply while the line is Planned (or a
counter-sales line) and can't drop below the delivered amount; price edits are kept as a
manual override unless they equal the resolved price (send `clearPriceOverride` to
revert). A configured (add-on) line's price is changed through the app. Lines on a
finalized invoice change only through Return Items. Notes may be edited even on billed lines.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from `GET /api/v1/jobs`.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Material line id (`items[].id` of the job).

404.description: No such job in your organization, or the line is not one of its live material lines.

422.description: The job is cancelled, the line is billed or configured, or the quantity/price is not allowed (the detail says which).

post.summary: Adds a labor line to a job.
post.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The customer rate is the
labor rate's hourly figure × `multiplier`; send `customerPrice` for $0-rate
variable-price labor. A cancelled job is read-only. The write is attributed to the key's creator.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id.

404.description: No job with this id in your organization.

422.description: The labor rate or task template is unknown, or the job is cancelled (the detail says which).

delete.summary: Removes a labor line from a job (soft delete).
delete.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. A line on a
finalized invoice can't be deleted (use Return Items); a cancelled job is read-only.
Totals are recomputed. The write is attributed to the key's creator.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id.

parameters.name: laborId
parameters.description: Labor line id.

200.description: The updated job with the labor line removed.

404.description: No such job in your organization, or the line is not one of its live labor lines.

422.description: The job is cancelled or the line is billed (the detail says which).

patch.summary: Edits a labor line's rate, hours and/or note.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. PATCH semantics. Changing
the rate resets the customer rate and clears any per-job price; recording actual hours
(> 0) marks the line completed. Lines on a finalized invoice change only through Return
Items (notes may still be edited). A cancelled job is read-only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id.

parameters.name: laborId
parameters.description: Labor line id (`labor[].id` of the job).

404.description: No such job in your organization, or the line is not one of its live labor lines.

422.description: The job is cancelled, the line is billed, or the labor rate is unknown (the detail says which).

get.summary: Lists a job's photos, newest first.
get.description:
Returns every `Photo` entry on the job's timeline — photos taken with the Flex field app's
