camera and photos added in the web app or with `POST /jobs/{id}/photos`. Signatures are not
photos and are not listed (they stay in the job's `updates`). All photos come back in one
page (`nextCursor` is always null). Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or
`?format=csv`). Needs `ViewJobs`. Example:
`curl https://app.flexonthejob.com/api/v1/jobs/42/photos -H "Authorization: Bearer flx_live_…"`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from a list response, e.g. `42`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

post.summary: Attaches a photo to a job; it appears on the job's timeline as a `Photo` entry.
post.description:
Send `multipart/form-data` with the image in a part named `file` and an optional
`caption` part, e.g.
`curl -X POST https://app.flexonthejob.com/api/v1/jobs/42/photos -H "Authorization: Bearer flx_live_…" -H "Idempotency-Key: 5f0c…" -F "file=@roof.jpg" -F "caption=Rust on the bottom panel"`.
JPEG and PNG only (detected from the file's bytes), up to 10 MB. The entry is attributed to the
key's creator and is the same kind of entry the Flex field app creates from the phone camera:
it shows as a thumbnail on the job's page in the web app, syncs to every device, and its image
is included in the organization data export. Needs `ManageJobs` — the same permission as
adding a job update in the app — and an `Idempotency-Key` header (a retry with the same
key and the same file replays the first response instead of adding a second photo).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from a list response, e.g. `42`.

file.description:
The photo, as a multipart file part named `file`. JPEG or PNG only — the type is read from
the file's leading bytes, not its name or declared content type. 1 byte to 10 MB (10,485,760 bytes).
Example: `-F "file=@roof.jpg"`.

caption.description:
Optional caption shown on the job's timeline, up to 2000 characters. Omitted or blank →
`Photo`. Example: `Rust on the bottom panel`.

201.description: The created timeline entry (`type` = `Photo`, `attachmentName` set). `Location` points at the job.

400.description: No `file` part, an empty file, a caption over 2000 characters, or a missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server or deactivated, or this server does not store photos (the demo sandbox).

413.description: The file is larger than 10 MB.

415.description: The file is not a JPEG or PNG image.

delete.summary: Deletes a photo from a job.
delete.description:
Removes a `Photo` entry from the job's timeline and deletes its image. `photoId` is the
`id` from `GET /jobs/{id}/photos`, the `id` of a `Photo` entry in the job's
`updates`, or the `id` returned by `POST /jobs/{id}/photos`. Only photos can be
deleted: signatures, notes and status changes are part of the job's record and answer 404. The
removal syncs to every device running a current Flex version (older installs keep the entry
until they update), and an internal note "Photo removed: …" attributed to
the key's creator is added to the timeline. Needs `ManageJobs`. Not idempotent-keyed: deleting
the same photo again answers 404. Example:
`curl -X DELETE https://app.flexonthejob.com/api/v1/jobs/42/photos/77 -H "Authorization: Bearer flx_live_…"`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id, e.g. `42`.

parameters.name: photoId
parameters.description: Photo id, e.g. `77`.

404.description: No such photo on this job in this organization (including signatures and other non-photo entries, and a photo already deleted).

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server or deactivated.

get.summary: Downloads a job photo's image.
get.description:
Streams the image bytes with `Content-Type``image/jpeg` or `image/png` (up to 10 MB).
`photoId` is the `id` from `GET /jobs/{id}/photos` (or of a `Photo` entry in the
job's `updates`). A photo taken on a phone becomes downloadable once that phone has synced
its upload; until then this answers 503. Needs `ViewJobs`. Example:
`curl https://app.flexonthejob.com/api/v1/jobs/42/photos/77/content -H "Authorization: Bearer flx_live_…" -o roof.jpg`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id, e.g. `42`.

parameters.name: photoId
parameters.description: Photo id from `GET /jobs/{id}/photos`, e.g. `77`.

404.description: No such photo on this job in this organization.

503.description: The image has not reached the server yet (a phone that has not synced) or storage is unreachable; retry later.

post.summary: Moves a scheduled job to a new start time (and optionally a new end).
post.description:
Requires the Scheduling module. Only jobs in `Scheduled` status — or draft /
estimated jobs that already carry a scheduled date — can be rescheduled; use
`POST /jobs/{id}/status` to schedule an unscheduled job first. Times are the
organization's local wall clock (`yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss`); a trailing `Z`
is converted to local time. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from a list response.

requestBody.description: New start, optional end and note.

403.description: Scheduling module not active for this organization.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

409.description: The job's status does not allow rescheduling, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

post.summary: Moves a job to another status.
post.description:
Name the target with `statusId` (one of the organization's status definitions)
or `statusKey` (a status definition name, or a system key such as
`InProgress` / `Completed`), not both. No transition rules are enforced —
any status may follow any other, exactly as in the UI. Requires an
`Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from a list response.

400.description: Neither or both of `statusId` / `statusKey`, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server, or the service refused the change.

422.description: Unknown status for this organization.

post.summary: Creates the job-site transfer for a job (the Job Details "Create Transfer" button).
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Same rules as
the button, which is only offered when the organization is not in counter-sales mode and the
job is `Estimated`, `Scheduled` or `InProgress`: stock is auto-selected for every `Planned` material line that still needs
delivery, the transfer is created `Pending` with the job's site location as its
destination, the job lines become `Reserved` and a "Transfer created" entry is added
to the job history. When the organization allows negative inventory a shortfall becomes a
stock-less line instead of an error. Returns the new transfer with its lines; its
`Location` header is `/api/v1/transfers/{transferId}`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id from `/api/v1/jobs`.

201.description: The created transfer.

404.description: No such job in this organization.

409.description: The organization is in counter-sales mode, the job is not `Estimated`/`Scheduled`/`InProgress`, the job has no job site location, no line needs transferring, no stock is available, or the key's creator is unknown on this server (detail says which).

500.description: The transfer could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

get.summary: Lists the organization's labor rates, one page at a time.
get.description:
Requires `ViewJobs`. Retired rates are excluded unless `includeInactive=true`.
Cursor-paginated: pass the last rate's `syncId` as `after`. Example:
`GET /api/v1/labor-rates?search=electrician`.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against name and description. Example: `electrician`.

parameters.name: includeInactive
parameters.description: Also return retired (inactive) rates (default `false`).

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only rates created or updated at/after this instant (ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor` (a labor-rate SyncId). Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1..200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

200.description: One page of labor rates and the cursor for the next page (null on the last page).

post.description:
Requires `ManagePurchaseOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "New Purchase
Order" in the app: the vendor must be active in your organization (or omit `vendorId` and
name a one-off vendor), the receiving location must be an active top-level location that is not
a job site, and each line names one of your items or bundles. The order and its lines are
written together or not at all. A new order is a `Draft`: move it along with
`/mark-ordered`, `/mark-shipped` and `/mark-delivered`, then `/receive` it.
Attributed to the key's creator. Example:
`{ "vendorId": 7, "receivingLocationId": 1, "lines": [ { "itemId": 12, "quantityOrdered": 24, "unitPrice": 3.10 } ] }`.

post.summary: Receives purchase-order lines into stock (the app's receiving panel).
post.description:
Requires `ManagePurchaseOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "lines": [ { "lineId": 1207, "quantity": 4 }, { "lineId": 1208, "quantity": 1, "locationId": 11 } ] }`.
Same code path and rules as receiving in the app: only an order whose `status` is
`Delivered` or `PartialReceived` can be received (409 otherwise, e.g. for a
`Cancelled`, `Ordered` or fully `Received` order); every line is checked before anything
is written (one bad line and nothing is received); a quantity above the line's
`quantityRemaining` is refused (over-receipt, also when a concurrent receipt of the
same line got there first); `locationId` defaults to the order's
`receivingLocationId`. An item line creates one stock item per unit at that location,
with the template's properties, barcodes and category, a `Cost` property from the
line's `unitPrice`, and `Shipping Cost` / `Total Cost` properties when the
line is on a shipment with a shipping cost; a bundle line creates one bundle per unit with
its items. The order `status` is then recomputed from its shipments: it becomes
`Received` when every unit is received and every shipment is delivered, otherwise
`PartialReceived`. The receipt is attributed to the key's
creator. Returns the order as `GET /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}` does.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Purchase-order id from `/api/v1/purchase-orders`. Example: `412`.

200.description: The purchase order after the receipt.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key`, or a malformed body (no lines, `quantity` below 1; fields listed in `errors`).

404.description: No such purchase order in this organization (or it is deleted).

409.description: The order is not `Delivered` or `PartialReceived` (detail: `Purchase order is Cancelled; only Delivered or PartialReceived orders can be received`), or the key's creator is unknown on this server. Nothing was received.

422.description: A line cannot be received: `Item not found in purchase order` (unknown `lineId`), `Cannot receive more than N remaining units` (over-receipt), or `Invalid destination location`; the offending field (e.g. `lines[0].quantity`) is listed in `errors`. Nothing was received.

`GET /api/v1/reorder-points` or `GET /api/v1/items/{id}/reorder-points`.

post.summary: Creates a custom role, like Roles → Create Role in the app.
post.description:
Requires `ManageRoles` and an `Idempotency-Key`. The name must be unique in the
organization (case-insensitive) and not a built-in role name; every permission must be a
FlexPermissions name held by both the API key and its creator. Assign it to accounts with
`customRoleId` / `customRoleIds` on `/api/v1/users`. Example:
`{ "name": "Dispatcher", "description": "Schedules crews", "permissions": ["ViewJobs", "ManageJobs"] }`.

201.description: Created; `Location` points at the new role.

403.description: A permission is not held by the key or its creator (listed in `errors`).

409.description: A role with this name already exists, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: A field is unacceptable (blank or long name, unknown permission); listed in `errors`.

delete.summary: Deletes a custom role, like Roles → Delete in the app.
delete.description:
Requires `ManageRoles` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The role and its permissions are
removed for good on the hosted web app and API (there is no restore); installed desktop and
back-office apps that sync the organization may keep listing it until they are reset. Built-in roles (`OrganizationAdmin`, `Manager`,
`User`) have no id and cannot be deleted. While any account (active or deactivated) still holds
the role the delete is refused with `409`, whose `detail` says how many; either remove it
from them first (`PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}` with the remaining `customRoleIds`) or repeat
with `?unassignUsers=true` to take it away from every account in the same call. Those accounts
are refused its permission-gated actions at once; menus in a signed-in browser session catch up
within about 5 minutes, and API keys minted by them lose the permissions within 60 seconds. A
`409` is stored against its `Idempotency-Key` for 24 hours like any other result, so
every retry after a `409` (whether you unassigned the holders first or add
`?unassignUsers=true`) needs a new `Idempotency-Key`; resending the old one replays the
`409`.
Example: `DELETE /api/v1/roles/4?unassignUsers=true`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Custom role id (from `GET /api/v1/roles`). Example: `4`.

parameters.name: unassignUsers
parameters.description: When `true`, remove the role from every account holding it and then delete it; when `false` (default) the delete is refused with `409` while any account holds it. Example: `true`.

200.description: Deleted; `id` is the deleted role and `message` names how many accounts lost it.

404.description: No such custom role in this organization (also built-in and already-deleted roles).

409.description: Accounts still hold the role and `unassignUsers` was not set, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The role could not be removed from an account or deleted; nothing after the failing step ran — retry.

get.summary: Returns one custom role.
get.description: Requires `ManageUsers`. Built-in roles have no id; read them from the list. Example: `GET /api/v1/roles/4`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Custom role id. Example: `4`.

404.description: No such custom role in this organization.

patch.summary: Edits a custom role; only the fields sent change.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageRoles` and an `Idempotency-Key`. `permissions` replaces the whole
set and takes effect for every account holding the role; each permission sent must be held by
both the API key and its creator. Built-in roles cannot be edited. Example:
`PATCH /api/v1/roles/4 { "permissions": ["ViewJobs"] }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Custom role id. Example: `4`.

403.description: A permission is not held by the key or its creator (listed in `errors`).

404.description: No such custom role in this organization.

409.description: Another role already has this name, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: A field is unacceptable; listed in `errors`.

get.summary: Lists the organization's sales orders, oldest first, one page at a time.
get.description:
Requires `ViewSalesOrders`. Pagination: pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `after`; `limit` defaults to 50 and is capped at 200. All
filters combine with AND. Example: `GET /api/v1/sales-orders?status=Pending&customerId=42`
lists customer 42's orders that are waiting to be fulfilled. Response carries a weak
`ETag`; resend it as `If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Order status to match exactly (case-insensitive): `Pending`, `Picking`, `Packed`, `Shipped`, `Delivered`, `Complete`, `Cancelled` (or the deprecated `Confirmed` of legacy rows). Example: `status=Pending`.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Only orders for this customer id. Example: `customerId=42`.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only orders created or modified (header or line edits, lines added or removed, status change, fulfilment and pick progress, `fulfillmentStatus` change) at or after this instant (ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`). Use it to poll for changes. Payments do not bump `updatedAt`: `paymentStatus`, `amountPaid` and `balanceDue` can change without it, so poll `/api/v1/invoices` (or re-read the order with `If-None-Match`) to follow payments.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor` (a sales-order SyncId). Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

200.description: A page of sales orders and the cursor for the next page (null on the last page).

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

400.description: Unknown `status` or unusable `after` cursor (field listed in `errors`).

post.summary: Creates a sales order, optionally with its lines (the app's New Sales Order page plus its item modal).
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "customerId": 42, "customerPONumber": "PO-7781", "lines": [ { "itemId": 5, "quantity": 10, "unitPrice": 125.00 } ] }`.
Same code path and defaults as the app: the order is created `Pending` with the next
`SO{yy}{MM}{nnnn}` number; `taxRate` omitted or 0 → the organization's default
rate, and 0 for a tax-exempt customer; `paymentTerms` omitted → the organization's
default terms; `orderDate` omitted → now. The customer must exist in this organization
and not be marked Difficult, `deliveryAddressId` must be one of its addresses and each
line's `itemId` a non-deleted catalog item — everything is checked before anything is
written. Lines are added as the app adds them: two lines for the same item become one line
(quantities add up; a later non-zero price or cost wins), line total = quantity × unit price,
then `subTotal`, `taxAmount` and `totalAmount` are computed. The order's
history records "Sales order created (via API key '…')". Creating reserves no stock; call
`POST /api/v1/sales-orders/{id}/fulfill` to start fulfilment.

201.description: Created; body is the order as `GET /api/v1/sales-orders/{id}` returns it, `Location` points at it.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key`, or a malformed body (`quantity` below 1, negative price, tax rate outside 0–100, more than 200 lines; fields listed in `errors`).

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server or belongs to another organization. Nothing was created.

422.description: Unknown or Difficult customer (`customerId`), an address that is not the customer's (`deliveryAddressId`) or an unknown item (`lines[i].itemId`). Nothing was created.

get.summary: Returns one sales order with its lines.
get.description:
Requires `ViewSalesOrders`. Removed lines are not returned. Response carries a weak
`ETag`; resend it as `If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id from the list endpoint. Example: `318`.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

patch.summary: Edits a sales order's header — the app's inline edits on the Details page (order number, PO, terms, dates, notes, tax rate, shipping cost).
patch.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Partial update:
omitted members are unchanged, `""` clears an optional text field,
`clearRequestedDeliveryDate: true` clears the date. Example:
`{ "shippingCost": 25.00, "taxRate": 8.25 }`. Same code path and rules as the Details
page: every field is checked before anything is written; a tax-rate or shipping change
recomputes `taxAmount` / `totalAmount` and the payment status and updates the
order's draft invoices (their subtotal, tax rate and "Shipping & Handling" line).
`updatedAt` moves; no history entry is written (as in the app). Complete and
Cancelled orders cannot be edited.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Updated; body is the order as `GET /api/v1/sales-orders/{id}` returns it.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key`, no field to change, `requestedDeliveryDate` sent with `clearRequestedDeliveryDate`, or a value out of range (fields listed in `errors`).

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The order is `Complete` or `Cancelled` (detail: `Cannot edit a cancelled or completed order`), or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Blank `orderNumber`, unknown `paymentTerms`, or a non-zero `taxRate` for a tax-exempt customer (field listed in `errors`). Nothing changed.

post.summary: Cancels a sales order (the app's Cancel page): delivered goods come back, transfers are cancelled.
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body optional:
`{ "reason": "Customer changed their mind" }`. Same code path as the app's Cancel
page: units already delivered by completed transfers are returned to inventory, live
transfers are cancelled and their reserved stock released, the order's lines are removed,
and the order and its payment status become `Cancelled` with the history entry
"Order cancelled by … (was …) (via API key '…')". `Cancelled` is terminal;
`Complete` and `Cancelled` orders are refused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Cancelled; `itemsReturned` and `transfersCancelled` say what was undone.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key` or a reason over 500 characters.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The order is already `Complete` or `Cancelled` (detail: `This order has already been completed or cancelled.`), or the key's creator is unknown.

500.description: Returning the stock or cancelling the transfers failed; everything was rolled back and the order is unchanged. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Marks a delivered sales order complete (the app's "Mark Complete").
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Only a
`Delivered` order can be completed; the history records "Order marked as complete
(via API key '…')". `Complete` is terminal. An order whose invoices are fully paid
may already have become `Complete` on delivery.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The order is not `Delivered` (detail: `Cannot transition from Shipped to Complete`), or the key's creator is unknown.

post.summary: Finishes picking a transfer (the scan dialog's "Complete"): the transfer leaves the warehouse (In Transit).
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body optional:
`{ "transferId": 904 }`; omitted = the order's single `Pending` transfer. Every
line of the transfer must be fully picked (`/pick`). The transfer becomes
`InTransit`, the history records "Transfer dispatched (via API key '…')" and the order's
`status` is recalculated — `Packed` once every line is picked and covered. Stock
stays reserved to the transfer until `/deliver`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Transfer in transit; the recalculated order status.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or `transferId` is not one of its transfers.

409.description: The transfer is not `Pending` (detail: `Transfer is already in InTransit status`), some lines are not fully picked (the detail names them), the order has no `Pending` transfer, or the key's creator is unknown.

422.description: Several `Pending` transfers and no `transferId` (`errors.transferId` lists them).

post.summary: Marks a shipped transfer delivered (the app's "Mark as Delivered"): its stock moves to the customer.
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body optional:
`{ "transferId": 904 }`; omitted = the order's single in-transit transfer. The transfer
must be in transit (at its last stop, if it has several) and have shipping info
(`/ship`). Same code path as the app: the transfer becomes `Completed`, each remaining
line's `quantityDelivered` is recorded, its stock units move to the delivery location and are
released — and consumed (removed from inventory) when that location's type consumes
inventory or is a job site, as customer delivery locations usually are. Lines marked
`Failed` in transit are not delivered: their units stay at their current location, are
released from the transfer, and the line ends `Returned` with no `quantityDelivered`
and a "[RETURNED] …" note on the item; lines already `Returned` are skipped. The history records
"Transfer completed — items delivered (via API key '…')" and the order's `status` is
recalculated: `Delivered` when every transfer is complete, or straight to
`Complete` when its invoices already cover the order and are paid.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or `transferId` is not one of its transfers.

409.description: The transfer is not in transit (detail: `Transfer must be In Transit to complete. Current status: …`), has waypoints left, has no shipping info yet, the order has no transfer in transit, or the key's creator is unknown.

422.description: Several transfers in transit and no `transferId` (`errors.transferId` lists them).

post.summary: Starts fulfilment of a sales order (the app's Begin Fulfillment button): creates the pick transfer.
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Same code
path and rules as the Begin Fulfillment button: the order must not be `Complete` or
`Cancelled`; a pick transfer is created from the order's source locations (else the
organization's warehouse locations) to its delivery destination for every line not yet covered, using
available stock; the history records "Fulfillment started (via API key '…')"; the order's
`status` is then recalculated — `Picking` when the transfers cover every line,
otherwise it stays `Pending` (call again once stock arrives). The response always
carries the real status; never assume `Picking`. Replaying the same
`Idempotency-Key` returns the first response. A call with a new key creates another
transfer only for the quantity not yet covered by a live (not Cancelled/Failed) transfer —
a partly covered line is topped up, never claimed twice — and is refused with 409
`Every line is already covered by a transfer` when nothing is left to cover, the same
rule that shows the Begin Fulfillment button in the app. Next steps: `/pick`,
`/complete-pick`, `/ship`, `/deliver`, `/complete`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id from `/api/v1/sales-orders`. Example: `318`.

200.description: Fulfilment started; the resulting status and the pick transfer id.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The order is `Complete` or `Cancelled` (detail: `Cannot transition from Complete to Picking`), every line is already covered by a transfer (detail: `Every line is already covered by a transfer`) or the order has no lines (`The order has no lines to fulfil`), the pick transfer could not be created (detail: `Error creating transfer: No source locations found for sales order`, or no available stock for any line), or the key's creator is unknown on this server. Nothing changed.

post.summary: Adds lines to an existing sales order (the app's item picker on the Details page).
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "lines": [ { "itemId": 5, "quantity": 2, "unitPrice": 125.00 } ] }`. Every line is
checked as on create (a non-deleted catalog item, quantity 1–1,000,000, price and cost
0–1,000,000,000) before anything is written; then the lines are added exactly as in the
app: a line for an item already on the order and not in a live transfer is merged into
it (quantities add up, a non-zero price or cost replaces the old one), totals and draft
invoices are recomputed and the history records "Added n item(s) (via API key '…')".
Adding lines reserves no stock; `/fulfill` (or `/transfers`) covers them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Added; body is the order with its lines.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key` or a malformed body (no lines, more than 200, values out of range).

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The order is `Complete` or `Cancelled`, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: An unknown, deleted or draft item (`lines[i].itemId`) or lines totalling more than 1,000,000,000,000. Nothing was added.

delete.summary: Removes a line from a sales order (the app's line remove button).
delete.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Only a
line that is on no live transfer can go — not even a completed one ("Cannot delete: item
is part of a transfer. Cancel the transfer first."); use `/returns` for delivered
goods. The line is soft-deleted (it disappears from `lines`), totals, payment status
and draft invoices are recomputed and the history records "Removed item '…'
(via API key '…')".

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

parameters.name: lineId
parameters.description: Line id. Example: `1502`.

200.description: Removed; body is the order with its remaining lines.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or the line is not one of its live lines (already removed).

409.description: The line is on a transfer, the order is `Complete` or `Cancelled`, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

patch.summary: Changes a line's unit price and/or unit cost (the app's inline price edit).
patch.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "unitPrice": 119.50 }`, `{ "unitCost": 80.00 }` or both. Same code path as the
Details page: the line total (quantity × price, less the line's discounts), the order's
`subTotal` / `taxAmount` / `totalAmount` and payment status are recomputed,
draft invoices are updated and the history records "Updated unit price on item '…'
(via API key '…')". Quantities cannot be changed (remove the line and add a new one).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

parameters.name: lineId
parameters.description: Line id (`lines[].id` of the order). Example: `1502`.

200.description: Updated; body is the order with its lines.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key`, neither field sent, or a value out of range.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or the line is not one of its (live) lines.

409.description: The order is `Complete` or `Cancelled`, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

post.summary: Picks one more unit of a line (the Fulfill page's per-line "Pick").
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Adds 1 to
the line's `quantityPicked` — a line-level count only: no stock unit or transfer
changes (the transfer scan flow is `/pick`). Refused once the line is picked in full.
`orderComplete` says whether every line is now picked.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

parameters.name: lineId
parameters.description: Line id. Example: `1502`.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or the line is not one of its live lines.

409.description: The order is `Complete` or `Cancelled` (detail: `Sales order is Cancelled; picking is closed.`), the line is already fully picked (detail: `Item '…' is already fully picked (10/10)`), or the key's creator is unknown.

put.summary: Sets a line's picked quantity (the Details page's picked-quantity editor); lowering it unpicks and releases stock.
put.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "quantityPicked": 3 }`. Only while the order is `Picking`. Same code path as
the app: raising the quantity claims that many more available units (the primary source
location and already-opened bundles first) onto the order's live transfer — or creates a
transfer for the uncovered remainder when there is none; lowering it takes units off the
live transfers (secondary locations first), releases them to stock and cancels a transfer
left empty. Over-picking is allowed. The order's `updatedAt` moves and a "Picking
progress — X of Y unit(s) picked" entry is written; the status does not change. This is
the line-level count; the transfer scan flow is `/pick`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

parameters.name: lineId
parameters.description: Line id. Example: `1502`.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key` or `quantityPicked` missing / out of range.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or the line is not one of its live lines.

409.description: The order is not `Picking` (detail: `Can only save picking progress when order is in Picking status`), a needed transfer could not be created (`Error creating transfer: …`), or the key's creator is unknown.

post.summary: Marks every line of a sales order picked in full (the Fulfill page's "Pick All").
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Each line's
`quantityPicked` is raised to its ordered quantity — a line-level count only, no stock
unit or transfer changes. `linesUpdated` is 0 when everything was already picked
(message `All items were already fully picked`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Picked; `linesUpdated` and `unitsAdded` say how much changed.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The order is `Complete` or `Cancelled` (detail: `Sales order is Complete; picking is closed.`), the order has no lines (detail: `No items found in this sales order`), or the key's creator is unknown.

post.summary: Picks a sales order's pick transfer — all of it (the app's "Pick All") or given units per line (the scan dialog).
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body optional:
`{}` or no body picks every line of the order's single `Pending` transfer in
full; `{ "transferId": 904, "lines": [ { "transferItemId": 5120, "quantity": 2 } ] }`
adds 2 to that transfer line's picked count (line ids: `lines[].id` of
`GET /api/v1/transfers/{transferId}`). Same code path as the app's transfer scan
dialog: the transfer line is stamped scanned by the key's creator and the order line's
`quantityPicked` rises by the same units. Every line is checked before anything is
written. Picking moves no stock and does not change the order's `status`; call
`/complete-pick` once every line is picked. Repeating a full pick is harmless; a
partial pick sent again with a new `Idempotency-Key` picks those units again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id from `/api/v1/sales-orders`. Example: `318`.

requestBody.description: Which transfer and, optionally, which lines.

200.description: Picked; `unitsPicked` says how many units this call picked.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or `transferId` is not one of its transfers.

409.description: The transfer is not `Pending`, the order has no `Pending` transfer, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: The order has several `Pending` transfers and `transferId` was omitted, or a line is not on the transfer, repeated, Returned/Failed, or asks for more units than are left to pick (field listed in `errors`). Nothing was picked.

get.summary: Lists what can still be returned from a sales order (the app's return modal).
get.description:
Requires `ViewSalesOrders` and `ManageReturns`. The order's completed transfers,
each with the stock units still at the customer (`items[].stockUnitId`) and the
untracked lines still returnable for value (`untrackedLines[]`). When a source
location was deleted, `needsReturnLocation` is true and `returnLocations` lists
where the units can go instead. Feed the ids to `POST …/returns`. Response carries a
weak `ETag`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: What is returnable (empty lists when nothing was delivered).

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

post.summary: Returns delivered goods of a sales order (the app's return modal): selected units, one transfer, or everything.
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders`, `ManageReturns` and an `Idempotency-Key`
header. Exactly one of: `{ "reason": "…", "stockUnitIds": [4410], "untrackedLines": [ { "transferItemId": 5121, "quantity": 1 } ] }`
(selective), `{ "reason": "…", "transferId": 904 }` (one completed transfer, which is
then cancelled) or `{ "reason": "…", "all": true }` (every completed transfer). Ids
come from `GET …/returnable-items`. Same code path as the app: returned units are
restored to stock at their source location (or `overrideLocationId` when it was
deleted), untracked lines are credited for value only, the order's lines and totals are
reduced, finalized invoice lines shrink, any overpayment becomes store credit on the
customer (`storeCreditIssued`), fully returned transfers are cancelled and the return
is logged with the reason and "(via API key '…')". The whole return is one transaction.
A unit already returned is skipped, so replaying with a new key returns nothing more
(409 `These items have already been returned.`). The order's `status` is not changed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Returned; counts, store credit and the order's status.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key`, no reason, or not exactly one of `all` / `transferId` / `stockUnitIds`+`untrackedLines`.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or `transferId` is not one of its transfers.

409.description: Nothing to return (`No items found to return.`, `These items have already been returned.`, `No completed transfers found.`, `Transfer not found or is not in Completed status.`), or the key's creator is unknown.

422.description: An `overrideLocationId` that is not one of `returnLocations` (`errors.overrideLocationId`).

500.description: The return failed part-way; everything was rolled back. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Picks one unit by barcode (the Fulfill page's scanner).
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "barcode": "0012345678905" }`. A stock unit's barcode picks the line pinned to that
unit; otherwise a catalog item's barcode picks the order's line for that item. The line's
`quantityPicked` rises by 1 — a line-level count only, no stock or transfer changes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Picked; the matched line's quantities and name.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The item is not on the order (detail: `Item '…' is not part of this sales order`), its line is already fully picked, the order is `Complete` or `Cancelled` (`… picking is closed.`), or the key's creator is unknown.

422.description: No stock unit or catalog item has this barcode (`errors.barcode`).

post.summary: Records the shipment of an in-transit transfer (the app's Ship dialog): carrier and tracking, or "ship without tracking".
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "transferId": 904, "carrier": "UPS", "trackingNumber": "1Z999AA10123456784" }`, or
`{ "transferId": 904, "withoutTracking": true }`. `transferId` omitted = the
order's single in-transit transfer. The transfer must be in transit (`/complete-pick`
first). Same code path as the app: the transfer's shipment is added — or replaced when it
already has one (every field is overwritten; `shipDate` omitted = now) — the history
records "Shipment added — UPS tracking … (via API key '…')" and the order's `status`
is recalculated: `Shipped` once every live transfer has shipping info. Without
tracking only flags the transfer shipped ("Shipped without tracking").

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Shipment saved; the recalculated order status.

400.description: Missing `Idempotency-Key`, a malformed body (a field over its length), or `withoutTracking` sent with shipment fields.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization, or `transferId` is not one of its transfers.

409.description: The transfer is not in transit (detail: `Shipping information can only be added while the transfer is In Transit. Current status: Pending`), the order has no transfer in transit, or the key's creator is unknown.

422.description: Several transfers in transit and no `transferId` (`errors.transferId` lists them).

post.summary: Creates another pick transfer for whatever lines are not yet covered (the app's "Create transfer").
post.description:
Requires `ManageSalesOrders` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Unlike
`/fulfill` it writes no status entry and works in any non-terminal status: the
transfer covers only the quantity of live lines not already on a live transfer, from the
order's source locations (else the warehouses), using available stock; the history
records "Transfer created (via API key '…')" and the order's `status` is recalculated.
Refused (409 `Error creating transfer: …`) when there is no source location or
nothing left to cover / no available stock. Next: `/pick`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sales-order id. Example: `318`.

200.description: Created; `transferId` is the new transfer, `status` the recalculated order status.

404.description: No such sales order in this organization.

409.description: The order is `Complete` or `Cancelled` (detail: `Cannot create transfer for order with status: Complete`), no transfer could be created, or the key's creator is unknown.

get.summary: Lists the jobs scheduled to start within a date range as calendar events.
get.description:
Times are the organization's local wall clock with no zone suffix
(`2026-09-08T00:00:00`); a trailing `Z` is converted to local time first.
The window may span at most 92 days. Events are not paginated — a quarter of jobs
is returned in one array. Response carries a weak `ETag`; resend it as
`If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive start of the window (required). Example: `2026-09-01T00:00:00`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive end of the window (required), at most 92 days after from. Example: `2026-09-30T23:59:59`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

400.description: Missing parameter, `to` before `from`, or a window longer than 92 days (field listed in `errors`).

403.description: Key lacks `ViewJobs` or the Scheduling module is not active.

get.summary: Lists schedule groups with their active members, one page at a time.
get.description:
Groups are flat with a `parentGroupId`; nest them client-side. Example:
`GET /api/v1/schedule-groups?parentGroupId=3` returns the crews of division 3.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: updatedSince

parameters.name: parentGroupId
parameters.description: Only direct children of this group; pass `0` for top-level groups only.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

post.summary: Creates a schedule group (a division, crew or team).
post.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as "New group" on the
Schedule Groups page: the group is placed last among its siblings. Add people with
`PUT /api/v1/schedule-groups/{id}/members/{userId}`.
Example: `{ "name": "Install Crew A", "colorHex": "#2e7d32", "parentGroupId": 3 }`.

delete.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The same soft delete as the
Schedule Groups page: the group and its memberships disappear, and jobs assigned under it keep
their assignees (only the group context on those assignments is cleared). Refused with
`409` while the group still has child groups — delete or move those first.

get.description: Send the previous `ETag` as `If-None-Match` to receive `304 Not Modified` when unchanged.

patch.summary: Edits a schedule group; only the fields sent change.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. `""` clears
`description` / `colorHex`; `"parentGroupId": 0` moves the group to the top level.
Moving a group under itself or one of its own crews is refused.
Example: `PATCH /api/v1/schedule-groups/7 { "name": "Crew A (North)" }`.

Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as saving the member
picker on the Schedule Groups page: listed users become (or stay) members, everyone else is

not an active user of this organization, or a lead missing from `userIds`, changes
nothing. Jobs already assigned are not changed. For single changes use
`PUT` / `DELETE .../members/{userId}`.
Example: `{ "userIds": ["3f2a…", "9b1c…"], "leadIds": ["3f2a…"] }`.

assigned to are not changed.

put.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The user must be an active
user of this organization (ids from `GET /api/v1/users`). A user may belong to several
groups. Example: `PUT /api/v1/schedule-groups/7/members/3f2a…` with `{ "isLead": true }`.

post.summary: Reorders the groups under one parent (sibling display order).
post.description:
Requires `ManageJobs` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Same as dragging groups on the
Schedule Groups page: `displayOrder` becomes 0, 1, 2, … in the order given. List every
group under the parent exactly once — a partial list is refused rather than half-applied.
Example: `{ "parentGroupId": 3, "ids": [9, 7, 8] }`.

get.summary: Lists the organization's inventory transfers, oldest first, one page at a time.
get.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` (the Transfers pages need it for reads too). Pagination:
pass the previous response's `nextCursor` as `after`; `limit` defaults to 50
and is capped at 200. All filters combine with AND. Example:
`GET /api/v1/transfers?jobId=1042&status=Pending`. The approval queue (what the
Pending Approvals page lists, and what `approve` / `reject` accept) is
`GET /api/v1/transfers?approvalStatus=Pending&status=Pending`. Response carries a weak
`ETag`; resend it as `If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.
Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Only transfers for this job id (see `/api/v1/jobs`).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Transfer status name to match exactly (case-insensitive), e.g. `Pending`, `InTransit`, `Completed`, `Cancelled`.

parameters.name: approvalStatus
parameters.description: Approval state to match exactly (case-insensitive): `Pending` (awaiting a decision), `Approved` or `Rejected`. Transfers that never needed approval are excluded whenever this is set. Example: `approvalStatus=Pending`.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only transfers created or modified at or after this instant (ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`). Use it to poll for changes.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor` (a transfer SyncId). Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–200 (default 50).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

200.description: A page of transfers and the cursor for the next page (null on the last page).

X-Next-Cursor.description: text/csv only: the page's nextCursor. Absent on the last page. Pass it as ?after= (or follow the Link header) to fetch the next page.

Link.description: text/csv only, alongside X-Next-Cursor: <absolute URL of the next page>; rel="next".

schema.description: CSV document: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting. The header row holds the JSON property names of one item (nested objects flattened as parent.child); one row per item of the page.

400.description: Unknown `status` or `approvalStatus`, or unusable `after` cursor (field listed in `errors`).

post.summary: Creates a standalone transfer of stock from one location to another (Transfers → Create).
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "sourceLocationId": 1, "destinationLocationId": 4, "notes": "Restock van 2", "lines": [ { "itemId": 12, "quantity": 3 } ] }`.
For each line the server picks the concrete units the way stock moves do: units of that item
at exactly `sourceLocationId` (not its child locations) that are not in transit, not in
a bundle and not already on an open transfer — fewest units consumed, then oldest first.
The units are grouped into transfer lines and the transfer is created `Pending`. When its
value reaches the organization's approval threshold it also gets an approval request
(`approvalStatus``Pending`, managers are emailed) and must be approved
(`POST /api/v1/transfers/{id}/approve`, which moves it straight to `InTransit`) or
rejected before anything else can happen. Otherwise the lifecycle is
`POST …/pick` → `POST …/start` → `POST …/complete` (or `POST …/cancel`
while `Pending`). Nothing is written unless every line can be filled. Returns the new
transfer; its `Location` header is `/api/v1/transfers/{id}`.

requestBody.description: Source, destination, optional notes and the lines to move.

201.description: The created transfer with its lines.

400.description: Malformed body (missing locations, no lines, more than 100 lines, quantity outside 1–1000) or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

409.description: Fewer available units at the source than a line asks for (detail names the item), or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: Unknown, foreign or inactive location, source equal to destination, or unknown / deleted item (field listed in `errors`, e.g. `lines[0].itemId`).

500.description: The transfer could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

get.summary: Returns one transfer with its item lines and approval state.
get.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers`. Response carries a weak `ETag`; resend it as
`If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Transfer id from the list endpoint.

404.description: No such transfer in this organization.

post.summary: Approves a transfer that is awaiting approval (Pending Approvals → Approve).
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Only a
transfer whose `approvalStatus` is `Pending` and whose `status` is still
`Pending` or `Draft` can be approved (list them with
`?approvalStatus=Pending&status=Pending`) — standalone
transfers whose value exceeded the organization's approval threshold; job-site transfers
never need approval. The transfer moves to `InTransit` and the requester is emailed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

200.description: Transfer id and confirmation message (`Transfer approved.`).

404.description: No such transfer in this organization.

500.description: The approval could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Cancels a job-site or standalone transfer and releases its stock.
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. A job-site
transfer (`isJobTransfer` true) is cancelled like the Job Details "Cancel" button: the
stock becomes available again, the job lines return to `Planned` and a "Transfer
cancelled" entry is added to the job history. A standalone transfer is cancelled like the
Transfers page's "Cancel Transfer" button, which is offered only while it is `Draft`, or
`Pending` and not awaiting approval (reject it instead). Sales-order transfers are
cancelled in the app.

post.summary: Completes (receives) an in-transit standalone transfer ("Complete Transfer"), optionally with lines that did not arrive.
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body optional:
`{ "failedLines": [ { "lineId": 911, "reason": "Damaged in transit" } ] }` marks those
lines failed first (the app's per-line "Mark as Failed"); they stay where they are and end
`Returned`. Every other unit moves to its line's destination, its in-transit flag is
cleared, `quantityDelivered` is recorded and the transfer becomes `Completed`
(the `transfer.completed` webhook fires). Only standalone transfers in an in-transit
status (`InTransit`, `InTransitToWaypoint`, `AtWaypoint`,
`InTransitToDestination`) can be completed; job-site and sales-order transfers are
completed from their job or order.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

200.description: Transfer id and confirmation message (e.g. `Transfer completed.`).

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Marks an in-transit standalone transfer failed (the Details page's "Mark as Failed").
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Only a
standalone transfer in `InTransit`. Its units keep their current location and their
in-transit flags are cleared; the transfer becomes `Failed`. To record that only some
lines failed, complete the transfer with `failedLines` instead.

parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

409.description: A job-site or sales-order transfer, not `InTransit`, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

patch.summary: Reduces the number of units one line moves.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "quantity": 2 }`. A line can only shrink (1 up to its current `quantity`): it keeps
its first units, the others are released and become available again, and
`quantityPicked` is capped at the new quantity. To move more, create another transfer —
growing a line could cross the approval threshold. Only on a standalone transfer that is
`Pending` and not awaiting approval, and only for a line that carries stock units.

parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

parameters.description: Line id (`lines[].id`).

404.description: No such transfer in this organization, or no such line on it.

409.description: A larger quantity than the line has, a line without stock units, not `Pending`, awaiting approval, a job-site or sales-order transfer, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Picks units of one line (the scan dialog's per-line pick).
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body optional:
`{ "quantity": 2 }` picks two more units; omit it to pick the rest of the line. Only on a
standalone transfer that is `Pending` and not awaiting approval. The line's
`quantityPicked` rises (never above `quantity`); once every line is fully picked the
transfer can be started (`POST …/start`). `POST …/pick` picks every line at once.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

parameters.name: lineId
parameters.description: Line id (`lines[].id` of `GET /api/v1/transfers/{id}`).

200.description: Transfer id and the line's progress (e.g. `Line 1207: 2 of 3 picked.`).

400.description: Malformed body, missing `Idempotency-Key`, or `quantity` outside 1–1000 (listed in `errors.quantity`).

404.description: No such transfer in this organization, or no such line on it.

409.description: Already fully picked or more units than are left, not `Pending`, awaiting approval, a job-site or sales-order transfer, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Redirects one line to another waypoint, the final destination or another location.
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "destinationType": "Location", "destinationId": 4, "reason": "Side entrance" }`. A
`Waypoint` target must be a `Pending` waypoint of this transfer (the line is then
dropped off there on arrival); `Destination` sends it to
the final destination; `Location` (an active location) makes that the line's own
destination when the transfer completes. The reason is noted on the line. The transfer must be a
standalone transfer that is `Pending` (not awaiting approval) or in transit, and the line
`Pending` or `InTransit` and not already dropped off at an `Arrived` /
`Departed` waypoint.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

parameters.name: lineId
parameters.description: Line id (`lines[].id`).

404.description: No such transfer in this organization, or no such line on it.

422.description: Missing `destinationType` or an unusable `destinationId` (field listed in `errors`).

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Removes picked units from one line (the scan dialog's unpick / reset).
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body optional:
`{ "quantity": 1 }` removes one picked unit; omit it to clear all of the line's picks.
Same state rule as `…/lines/{lineId}/pick`. At 0 picked the line is no longer marked scanned.

parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

parameters.name: lineId
parameters.description: Line id (`lines[].id`).

200.description: Transfer id and the line's progress (e.g. `Line 1207: 1 of 3 picked.`).

400.description: Malformed body, missing `Idempotency-Key`, or `quantity` outside 1–1000 (listed in `errors.quantity`).

404.description: No such transfer in this organization, or no such line on it.

409.description: Nothing picked on the line or more units than are picked, not `Pending`, awaiting approval, a job-site or sales-order transfer, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Marks every line of a standalone transfer fully picked (the scan dialog's "Pick All").
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Only for a
standalone transfer that is `Pending` and not awaiting approval — the only state in
which the app offers scanning. Each line's `quantityPicked` becomes its `quantity`;
the transfer can then be started. Picking again is harmless ("Every line was already fully picked.").

parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

404.description: No such transfer in this organization.

409.description: A job-site or sales-order transfer, a transfer awaiting approval or no longer `Pending`, or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Rejects a transfer that is awaiting approval (Pending Approvals → Reject).
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body:
`{ "reason": "Van 2 is out of service this week." }` — the reason is required. Only a
transfer whose `approvalStatus` is `Pending` and whose `status` is still
`Pending` or `Draft` can be rejected. The transfer is
cancelled, the reason is stored as `rejectionReason` and the requester is emailed.

parameters.description: Transfer id from `/api/v1/transfers`.

409.description: The transfer has no pending approval (none requested, already decided, or the transfer was since cancelled, completed or moved), or the key's creator is unknown on this server.

500.description: The rejection could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Scans a barcode into a transfer (the scan dialog): one more unit picked on the matching line.
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header (use a new key per scan —
a replayed key does not scan again). Body: `{ "barcode": "0012345678905", "locationId": 1 }`.
The barcode may be a unit's barcode or an item template's; the first line of that item (at
`locationId` when given) that is not fully picked gets one more picked unit. Same state
rule as `…/lines/{lineId}/pick`.

422.description: No item or item template has the barcode (`barcode` in `errors`).

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Starts a picked standalone transfer ("Mark as In Transit").
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. The transfer
must be a standalone transfer, `Pending`, not awaiting approval, and every line fully
picked (`POST /api/v1/transfers/{id}/pick`). The transfer and its lines become
`InTransit` and its units are flagged in transit until it is completed or failed.

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Submits a Draft standalone transfer (the Details page's "Submit Transfer"): it becomes Pending.
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. Only a
standalone transfer in `Draft` (transfers created by `POST /api/v1/transfers` are
already `Pending`). The approval rule of a new transfer applies: when its value reaches
the organization's threshold an approval is requested (`approvalStatus``Pending`,
managers are emailed) and only approve / reject apply until it is decided.

500.description: The change could not be saved. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

post.summary: Arrives at a waypoint: the lines assigned to it are dropped off there.
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. The transfer must
be a standalone transfer in an in-transit status and the waypoint (`waypoints[].id`)
`Pending`. The units of every line whose `destinationWaypointId` is this waypoint move
to its location (with their bundles); the waypoint becomes `Arrived` and the transfer
`AtWaypoint`. The final destination is reached with `POST …/complete`.

post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. The waypoint must
be `Arrived` (the stock already moved on arrival); a "Delivered at …" note is added to each
of its lines. Same transfer rule as `…/arrive`.

post.summary: Departs from an arrived waypoint towards the next stop.
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header; no body. The waypoint must
be `Arrived`; it becomes `Departed` and the transfer `InTransitToWaypoint` (heading
to the next waypoint, `currentWaypointId`) or `InTransitToDestination`. Same transfer
rule as `…/arrive`.

post.summary: Skips a waypoint, redirecting the lines still assigned to it (Skip Waypoint).
post.description:
Requires `ManageTransfers` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Body (required when lines
are still to be dropped off there): `{ "destinationType": "Waypoint", "destinationId": 42 }`
(a later `Pending` waypoint), `{ "destinationType": "Destination" }` or
`{ "destinationType": "Location", "destinationId": 4 }` (an active location, added as a
drop-off waypoint at the end of the route). The waypoint must be `Pending` (an
`Arrived` one already had its lines dropped off - leave it with `…/depart`); it becomes `Skipped` and the transfer moves on to the next `Pending`
waypoint or `InTransitToDestination`. Same transfer rule as `…/arrive`.

get.summary: Lists the organization's users with the schedule groups each belongs to.
get.description: Users are keyed by string ids, so this collection is not cursor-paginated: the whole list is returned in one response (ordered by first then last name) with `nextCursor` always `null`. The response carries an `ETag`; send it as `If-None-Match` to get `304` when nothing changed. Example: `GET /api/v1/users?scheduleGroupId=5` returns the members of group 5. Also available as CSV (`Accept: text/csv` or `?format=csv`); paging cursor in `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.description: Also return deactivated accounts (default `false`).

parameters.description: Alternative to the Accept header: `csv` returns text/csv.

post.summary: Creates an account in the organization, like Users → Add User in the app.
post.description:
Requires `ManageUsers` and an `Idempotency-Key`. The sync server creates the account
(the same call the Add User page makes); it can sign in to the web app at once and on devices at
their next sign-in. The key's creator must be an OrganizationAdmin (or higher); `role` may be
at most the creator's own; SystemAdmin is never assignable; and every permission the new account
would get (its role's, plus `customRoleId`'s) must be held by the API key and by its creator.
The password must meet the Flex password rule and is never returned. An active account counts as
a billed seat once the organization is past its included seats. Example:
`{ "email": "sam@example.com", "firstName": "Sam", "lastName": "Carter", "password": "Welcome#2026", "role": "Manager" }`.

201.description: Created; `Location` points at the new account.

202.description: The sync server created the account but this host has not received it yet (it appears after the next sync).

400.description: Malformed body, an unknown `role`, or missing `Idempotency-Key`.

403.description: A hierarchy or grant rule refused it (the detail says which).

409.description: The key's creator is unknown on this server.

422.description: A value is unacceptable: e-mail already in use, weak password, unknown `customRoleId`.

502.description: The sync server answered with an unexpected error.

503.description: This server cannot reach the sync server (not registered or offline); nothing was created.

get.summary: Returns one account with its roles and effective permissions.
get.description:
Requires `ManageUsers` (no module). Sends a weak `ETag`. Example:
`GET /api/v1/users/8f0c3c1e-2b6d-4c55-9a51-0d3f3c1b7e21`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: User id (string GUID) from `GET /api/v1/users`.

patch.summary: Edits an account; only the fields sent change.
patch.description:
Requires `ManageUsers` and an `Idempotency-Key`. The account must belong to the
organization, must not be the key creator's own, and must hold a strictly lesser role than the
creator (an OrganizationAdmin manages Managers and Users). `role` may rank up to the creator's
own, so an OrganizationAdmin can promote a Manager or User to `OrganizationAdmin`. `role` and `isActive` go through the sync server like the user list's buttons;
names and `customRoleIds` are written here. Whatever the edit adds to the account's
permissions (all of them when it reactivates the account) must be held by the API key and its
creator. Demoting or deactivating an Organization Admin is refused (403): use
`POST /api/v1/users/{id}/removal-requests` (their approval or 14 days' notice). Every rule is
checked before anything changes. Example:
`PATCH /api/v1/users/8f0c3c1e-2b6d-4c55-9a51-0d3f3c1b7e21 { "role": "Manager", "customRoleIds": [4] }`.
